title: Associated points of monoidal centers lie over log-stratum generic points
statement:
Let $(X,M)$ be a Noetherian fs log regular scheme [def-trf-fs-log-blowup], [pqf-def-locnoeth]. Write $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$ for the set of generic points of the log strata, the connected components of the constant-rank loci of $\overline M^{\rm gp}$. For a Noetherian scheme $Z$, an associated point of a coherent module $H$ means a point $z$ for which the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Z,z}$ annihilates a nonzero element of $H_z$.

(i) For every nonempty coherent log ideal $\mathcal I\subset M$, set $J=\alpha(\mathcal I)\mathcal O_X$. Every associated point of $\mathcal O_X/J$ lies in $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$. If $V(J)$ is nonempty, this associated-point set is nonempty.

(ii) For a saturated log blowup $b:(X',M')\to(X,M)$, every point of $\operatorname{Fan}(X',M')$ maps into $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$.

(iii) In any finite saturated log blowup tower over $(X,M)$, with log centers $\mathcal I_i$ and underlying scheme ideals $J_i$, the images in $X$ of all associated points of $\mathcal O_{X_i}/J_i$ lie in $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$. The statements are etale local; for a Zariski log structure this set is finite and is the canonical fan with its induced topology and characteristic monoid sheaf. No excellence or characteristic hypothesis is required. Noetherian schemes here admit finite affine covers by spectra of Noetherian rings.

source.place: VIII 3.4.11 and Lemma 3.4.13(i)--(iii), with the saturated case in its proof, printed pp.112--113 No Stacks tag states this combined result; the cited place is in the archived ILO volume.

proof.text: Use the regular rank-stratum local model: at a geometric point $\bar x$ the stratum has strict local ring $A/I_x$, and $x\in\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$ exactly when this is a field. This condition is invariant under strict etale restriction. Associated points of the quotient by the algebraized ideal are invariant under the same restriction, by etale assassin invariance; the chart construction identifies its restriction with the quotient by the chart monomials. Thus (i) and (ii) can be checked on pointed etale chart neighbourhoods. The characteristic sheaf and the monoidal ideal, not an auxiliary choice of chart, determine these conditions.

source.place: VI 1.2, 1.5; VIII 3.4.11 and beginning of proof of 3.4.13(i), pp.112--113.

proof.text: Fix $x\notin\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$ and write $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$, $A=R^{\rm sh}$ and $T=\widehat A$. Strict henselization is faithfully flat and Noetherian; its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_RA$. Its completion is faithfully flat and its maximal ideal is $\mathfrak m_AT$. If $x$ were associated to $\mathcal O_X/J$, there would be an injection $R/\mathfrak m_R\hookrightarrow(R/J_x)$. Flatness preserves that injection first over $A$ and then over $T$. Consequently $T/J_xT$ would contain a nonzero element annihilated by the maximal ideal of $T$. These are applications of the defining exactness of tensoring with a flat module, not an assertion that arbitrary points over associated points remain associated.

source.place: VIII 3.4.13(i), completion reduction, p.112; Stacks Tags 07QM, 06LJ, 04GP, 05GG and 05GI.

proof.text: Choose the sharp chart supplied by the completed-chart theorem. In equal characteristic, $T=k[[Q]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]$; in mixed characteristic, $T=C[[Q]][[t_1,\ldots,t_n]]/(\theta)$ with $\theta\equiv p$ modulo nonzero monomials and the $t_i$. The coherent log ideal in this chart is generated by finitely many monomials, hence $J_xT$ is the ideal of a monoid ideal $H\subset Q$. Units multiplying a monomial generator do not change that ideal. Here $n\ne0$: if $n=0$, the quotient of $T$ by its nonunit log monomials is $k$ in equal characteristic, and $C/(p)$ in mixed characteristic. The maximal ideal of $A/I_x$ would then become zero under the faithfully flat map to that field (the completed maximal ideal is extended from $A$); it is therefore zero already. This would make $A/I_x$ a field and put $x$ in the fan. Thus $n\geq1$.

source.place: VI 1.6, p.70; VIII 3.4.13(i), p.112, including the explanation of n >= 1.

proof.text: The transverse-parameter lemma makes multiplication by $t_1$ injective on $T/J_xT$, both for the equal-characteristic model and for the mixed-characteristic equation quotient. But $t_1$ lies in the maximal ideal of $T$. It cannot annihilate the nonzero element obtained in step 2. This contradiction proves that no $x$ outside the fan is associated to $\mathcal O_X/J$, establishing the containment in (i).

source.place: VIII 3.4.13(i), p.113; the parameter argument replaces the equivalent depth formulation.

proof.text: If $V(J)\ne\varnothing$, choose a Noetherian affine open $W=\operatorname{Spec}D$ meeting it. The chart construction makes $J$ a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal, so the quotient on $W$ is $D/K$ for a proper ideal $K$. This module is nonzero, and $0$ is a zerodivisor on it. The zerodivisor/associated-prime equality therefore gives a prime in $\operatorname{Ass}_D(D/K)$. The affine associated-point dictionary gives an associated point of $\mathcal O_X/J$ in $W$. This proves the nonemptiness assertion without any excellence assumption.

source.place: VIII 3.4.13(i), p.112; elementary nonemptiness consequence of Stacks Tags 00L9/05BV and 02OK (using the cited zerodivisor equality).

proof.text: For (ii), use the saturated-blowup chart cover at a chosen point of $X'$. It gives etale-local compatible fs charts $P\to Q$ with isomorphic group completions and identifies the source with the ordinary chart fibre product. Identifying those groups makes $P\subset Q\subset P^{\rm gp}$, with $Q$ finitely generated and saturated. The toric-refinement theorem says that this chart source is locally Noetherian and log regular; the chart sources cover $X'$. Thus $X'$ is log regular, and the fan criteria of step 1 apply to both sides. Reduce to a point $y$ of one such affine chart, with image $x$.

Put $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$ on the chosen chart and let $B$ be the local ring at $y$ of $\operatorname{Spec}(R\otimes_{\mathbf Z[P]}\mathbf Z[Q])$. Set $G=\{p\in P:\alpha(p)\in R^	imes\}$ and $F=\{q\in Q:z^q\in B^	imes\}$. Products are units only when both factors are units, so these are faces and $F\cap P=G$. Let $I=(\alpha(p):p
otin G)R$ and $K=(z^q:q
otin F)B$. Inverting $F$ and killing its complement sends $z^f$ to its group monomial for $f\in F$ and all other monomials to zero. This is multiplicative since $F$ is a face. Tensor balancing kills exactly the images of $p
otin G$ in $R$ and identifies the two images of $G^{m gp}$. The inverse sends $ ar r\otimes z^f$ to the class of $rz^f$. Localizing these inverse maps at the prime of $y$ gives
$$B/K\simeq\left((R/I)\otimes_{\mathbf Z[G^{m gp}]}\mathbf Z[F^{m gp}]ight)_{\mathfrak q}.$$
By the rank-stratum model $R/I$ and $B/K$ are the ordinary local rings of the respective rank strata.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.13(ii), p.113; explicit face-stratum algebra, avoiding the printed repeated quotient by f.

proof.text: Face sharpening gives that $P^{\rm gp}/G^{\rm gp}$ is finite free. Its subgroup $F^{\rm gp}/G^{\rm gp}$ is therefore finite free. Choose a basis and lift it to $F^{\rm gp}$; this splits the group extension. The tensor ring in step 7 becomes a Laurent polynomial ring over $R/I$, by sending each lifted basis element to a Laurent variable and its inverse to the inverse variable. Now $R/I$ is a regular local domain. The Laurent polynomial ring is a domain (compare the leading terms of finite Laurent sums), and its localization at $\mathfrak q$ contains $R/I$ injectively. Since $R\to B$ is local, $\mathfrak q$ contracts to the maximal ideal of $R/I$. If that ideal had a nonzero element, its image would be a nonzero nonunit of $B/K$; thus $B/K$ could not be a field. Hence $y$ generic in its stratum, equivalently $B/K$ a field, forces $R/I$ to be a field, equivalently $x$ generic in its stratum. Etale invariance from step 1 gives (ii) on the original schemes.

source.place: VIII proof of 3.4.13(ii), p.113; elementary Laurent-stratum variant of the completed-chart argument.

proof.text: Induct on the length of the saturated blowup tower. The length-zero composition maps the fan of $X$ to itself. At each successor stage, step 6 supplies a locally Noetherian log regular source and (ii) maps its fan into the preceding fan. Composition therefore maps every stage fan into $\operatorname{Fan}(X,M)$. The containment proof of (i) was pointwise and used no quasi-compactness, so it applies on every such stage. Apply that containment at the stage of each center: its associated points lie in that stage fan, so their images lie in the fan of $X$. This proves (iii), including towers of length zero and unit centers. Etale-locality follows from step 1 and the strict etale chart construction for blowups.

source.place: VIII 3.4.13(iii), final sentence of proof, p.113; strict etale compatibility in 3.3.8--3.3.11.

proof.text: For a Zariski log structure, use the local face models of the regular rank strata. Their homeomorphisms identify the induced-topology stratum-generic-point set locally with $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P$, and their characteristic stalks and generization maps identify the restricted characteristic sheaf with the sharp monoid-spectrum sheaf. These identifications are restrictions of the same characteristic sheaf on $X$, so they agree on overlaps. They give precisely the affine charts required in the definition of a fine fan. The rank-stratum model also gives finitely many ranks and finitely many connected components in each rank for Noetherian $X$, so this fan has finitely many points. All inputs used only fs log regularity and Noetherianity, not excellence or a characteristic restriction.

proof_origin.place: VIII 3.4.11 and proof of Lemma 3.4.13, pp.112--113; VI 1.2,1.5--1.6, pp.69--70. Face-stratum algebra expands the saturated part of (ii).
